identification: Keen's Genuine Tasmanian Curry Powder 4 oz canister, Keen's Curry Powder Co., Kingston, Brown's River; purple and gold paper label citing the 1866-7 Intercolonial Exhibition medal; reverse recipe panel mentions Keen's Tasmanian Sauce. Probably early 20th century (before the 1954 sale to Reckitt & Colman); the 1866-7 date on the label is the medal, not the tin's date. Torn label, rust at rims.
searches_tried: comps.py (work/ and pipeline/) for keen's curry, keens curry powder, curry tin, keen: no sold same-item hits (only a Gowans Apr 2026 lot 'KEENS CURRY PHOTOGRAPHS & BADGES' at $2 hammer, a different item). Gowans API search for keens/keen's/curry powder: no tin. WebSearch x5 (Armitage past lots, Gowans, general auction, antique price, vintage for sale): only modern retail tins (about A$24 for 250g) and history pages, no vintage tin sale or asking price found. eBay sold listings would settle it best (closed to us).
chrome_hint: eBay AU sold listings: 'Keens curry tin' and 'Keen's Tasmanian curry powder tin Kingston Brown's River' (sold items, last 12 months); also Trade Me completed and Invaluable/LiveAuctioneers 'Keen's curry tin'.
viewing_check: Check the label printing and any date or size marks (4 oz nett), how much label is missing or torn, whether the base and lid have pinholes from rust, and whether any contents remain. Compare against other vintage Keen's tins if seen at the viewing.
rate_note: No priced entries, so no exchange rate used.
